# Issue review

## Scope

Reviewed all **122 issues: 44 open and 78 closed**. Cross-checked the code on `main`, the `fetcher` branch, tests, and GitHub statuses. All GitHub statuses matched the local notes.

This document preserves the review from September 12, 2026; it was not rerun on the file creation date:

- `main`: `26915194e4bd196ea22fd38f270f3d2722d804dd`.
- `fetcher`: `1a7e92a` (`docs(status): explain push lock column and JSON filtering`).

“Relevant” means work remains; this review does not assess priority. “Partial” means some of the expected behavior is implemented. “Needs clarification” means there is insufficient evidence either to close the issue or to start implementation. Closure as `not planned` does not mean the behavior was fixed.

Clarification: [[issue-64|#64]] and [[issue-98|#98]] are already partially implemented in `fetcher`, although those changes are absent from the reviewed `main`.

## Validation and sources

- The local build, `go build -o /tmp/maintainer-relevance-cli .`, passed.
- Tests passed for `./internal/model/github/contribution`, `./internal/command/github/contribution`, `./internal/pkg/time`, `./internal/config`, `./internal/model/golang/vanity`, and `./internal/pkg/io`.
- Temporary checks outside the repository confirmed the defects in [[issue-70|#70]], [[issue-133|#133]] / [[issue-148|#148]], [[issue-155|#155]], [[issue-189|#189]], and [[issue-284|#284]]. Nested Makefile includes, weekly windows, future-day markers, and the date selection scenario from [[issue-119|#119]] were also checked.
- Fresh public HTML for the `kamilsk` contribution calendar for 2021 parsed successfully: 365 days, totaling 1450 contributions. This validates that specific calendar; it does not guarantee resilience to all HTML changes.
- According to the [release list](https://github.com/octomation/maintainer/releases), the latest published tag at the time of review was `v0.1.0-rc11`; there was no `v0.1.0` release.
- The [fetcher branch](https://github.com/octomation/maintainer/tree/fetcher) implements fetch, workspace, offline status with a TUI, and contribution retrieval through GraphQL. Repository discovery uses REST; the GraphQL discoverer remains a stub.
